In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the effects of TG and CPA on twitch force and SR Ca2+ content are complex, and depend on many factors.
TG is an excellent inhibitor of SR Ca2+, but only in single myocytes.
TG and CPA are effective SR Ca2+ pump blockers in multicellular preparations, but the effects are not as pronounced as in single myocytes or isolated membranes.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
TG and CPA are not good tools for studying SR Ca2+ release in multicellular preparations, and the effects of TG and CPA on twitch force and twitch duration are not necessarily mediated by the SR.
TG and CPA are effective in blocking SR Ca2+ transport, but that this is incomplete in multicellular cardiac preparations and that the effects on contractile force and Ca2+ transient are complex.
TG and CPA can be used as SR Ca2+ pump inhibitors in multicellular preparations but only at concentrations that do not completely abolish SR Ca2+ release.
The main takeaway from our work is that
TG and CPA can be used to block the SR Ca2+, but only if the SR Ca2+-uptake mechanism is not fully blocked.
TG and CPA are not good tools for studying the effects of Ca2+ pump blockade in intact multicellular preparations.
TG is a useful tool for studying SR function in cardiac preparations, provided its effect is evaluated by RCCs or similar methods.
